title: the six characters' graphics pass on top of cast A (faces, hair, beards, bodies, clothes, shoes, the driving hands)
lensAText: a sceptical game art director and character artist. Open the owner's sheets in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/0N-name/ (body-sheet.webp, face-sheet.webp) with the Read tool and compare them with the builder's -fx renders and its BEFORE images: is each of the six now clearly THAT person up close (picker turntable, third person) and at game distance (crowds): face shape and features, skin tone, hair silhouette (no helmets), beard (soft-edged cards, no box at yaw 45-90 deg, no grey speckle at distance), Marcus's right-eyebrow scar and muscular build, the other builds, shoulders, sleeves, trouser fit, shoes, accessories? Is it a clear step up from BEFORE, consistent in style across the six and with the existing NPCs, free of artefacts (gaps, clipping, z-fighting, hard alpha edges, broken hair or cloth)? Did any existing non-cast person get worse? Then take your own frames in ONE short Playwright script on dist/artifact.html: the main menu's Character entry and the picker at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, DPR 3) and 1450x767; pick two different characters, walk in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time (via Go To, Get out) and look at the avatar and the crowd up close; the seat view in the Rossini GT for two characters (their own cuffs and skin tone). ALSO: drive 60 s in the seat view steering to full lock both ways at 390x844 DPR 3 and watch for hand or arm clipping, sleeve popping, z-fighting, flicker, shimmer or stutter; check the builder's alternating frame-time table for plausibility against one short measurement of your own (CDP CPU throttle 4). Stylised real-time 3D is the target, not photoreal: reject for defects and for failing to read as the person, not for being stylised.
brief: THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~11:00 PM PT) pasted this Fable prompt to run now: "Fable prompt — OC Ultra (top-speed-ultra), the six characters' graphics pass. Branch claude/cast (worktree tsu-cast). Read CLAUDE.md, PROJECT_OC_CAST.md and PROJECT_OC_HANDOFF.md ('the six characters' graphics pass'). Files: src/onfoot/people/* incl. face.ts, skin.ts, masks.ts, body.ts (coordinate with the session that owns them); the six are in src/onfoot/cast.ts. Fix against the owner's sheets: generic faces with dark smudges on cheeks/jaw, helmet-like wavy and side-part hair, sloping shoulders, Marcus not muscular, the beard (strand cards with a soft alpha edge), Marcus's scar on his RIGHT eyebrow. Keep existing presets, the public API and the LOD budgets (phone 2,500 / 14,000 / 90,000 tris). Proof: node tests/cast-shoot.mjs + python3 tests/cast-sheets.py <sheets folder> beside the sheets; npm test -- --only=cast,cast-venues; each venue's crowd frames. Log in PROJECT_OC_PROGRESS.md and PROJECT_OC_CAST.md." STATE: HEAD is 224a906, a LOCAL commit (not pushed, not yet judged) of the first cast-A build on top of 5cf7212 (the live v15): read 'git show --stat 224a906', PROJECT_OC_CAST.md and the cast entry at the top of PROJECT_OC_PROGRESS.md first; that build's own report of what is right and wrong is there (system parts done: catalog, picker on the main menu, driver match, crowds from the six, pack scaffold, full-lock fix; look not done). The sheets folder is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters (0N-name/body-sheet.webp and face-sheet.webp; open them with the Read tool). COORDINATION (settled with the session that owns people/*, 2026-11-12 ~07:00 UTC): this pass MAY edit face.ts, skin.ts, masks.ts and body.ts. That session's own face work never landed and is unjudged: branch fable/face b5ac6a2 (teeth as crowns, beard/goatee/moustache strand cards, the smile reaching cheeks and eyes, eyes set in their sockets with lid shade, a cheaper phone skin shader, mouth corners without pits) and on top fable/face-r3-wip 9a1a8af (its unfinished round 3: the beard side mask as smooth ramps stopping before the ear, the neck step, a ragged beard-tint edge, a leaf people/morphs.ts for an import cycle, tapered tufts, a brow guard band). Its re-judge said revise: (sev 3) full-beard men at yaw >= 45 deg show the beard as a hard-edged dark box over cheek, jaw and the front of the ear (very likely our 'dark smudges on cheeks and jaw'); (sev 2) greying beards over dark hair speckle at game distance. Its full defect list: 'git show origin/claude/hypercar:top-speed-ultra/PROJECT_OC_HANDOFF.md', section 'Face/eyes (fable/face ...)'. STEP 1, the ONE git operation allowed in this build: 'git fetch origin fable/face-r3-wip' then 'git merge origin/fable/face-r3-wip' (it branches from 5229abf; it touches only people/face.ts, head.ts, masks.ts, morphs.ts (new), skin.ts and src/onfoot/test-people.ts); resolve conflicts keeping BOTH the cast lane's additive features and the face work; once npx tsc --noEmit passes, commit the merge (message 'Merge fable/face-r3-wip (unjudged face rounds 1-3) into claude/cast', ending with the line 'Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01NkQ41gebWX6mPbmCQZBc81'). Everything after that stays UNCOMMITTED for the judges. STEP 2: finish that face work's round 3 and fix its open defects (the beard box at yaw >= 45 deg, the grey-beard speckle at game distance, anything else its handoff section lists), with before/after heads at yaw 0, 45 and 90 deg. Every person in the game uses these files, so the improvement reaches every NPC; keep each existing preset's parameters and the public API, and check one existing non-cast preset's head before/after for regressions. STEP 3: the six against their sheets, at close range (the picker turntable, third person in a venue) and at game distance: (a) faces: each face's own shape and features read as that person (Mateo's broad jaw and short boxed beard, Danny's slim face and glasses, Marcus's strong jaw, full greying beard and the scar on his RIGHT eyebrow as a FaceShape parameter or a decal, Leila's features, Jas's youthful face, Kate's freckles); no smudges; (b) hair: the shoulder-length waves (Leila) and side-part undercut (Danny) must not read as helmets: a broken silhouette with layered locks, volume at the ends, a parting; Jas's high ponytail, Kate's low ponytail and Mateo's skin fade with a textured top readable; no slabs, gaps or broken strands; (c) beards as strand cards with a soft alpha edge (build on the face branch's cards), no hard shell, no tabs at the ears; (d) bodies: shoulders at the right width and slope, Marcus clearly muscular (chest, shoulders, arms), the builds differ (Mateo stocky, Danny slim, Jas petite, Kate tall); (e) clothes: no ballooning sleeves (the shoulder seam at the shoulder point, the sleeve tapering to the cuff), collars and lapels where the builder can, jeans, work pants, cargo pants and tailored trousers with a straight or relaxed leg (not leggings; Kate's cargo pockets visible), Mateo's jacket zip-front per the image; (f) shoes that read as those shoes from the side and front (Mateo's work boots, Kate's boots, Jas's chunky sneakers, Leila's low heels; sole, heel, ankle height, toe shape), not flat slippers. Quality tiers: HD and Ultra get the full detail (skin shading, hair cards, cloth folds and fabric); Low stays cheap for phones. Keep the builder's LOD budgets (phone 2,500 / 14,000 / 90,000 tris) and the crowd draw-call counts. STEP 4, the driving hands (the owner: 'make sure the driver matches to the player'): the hands' owner agreed that we add, in src/preview/hands-acc.ts ONLY and additively behind NEW option values (existing defaults and options unchanged; no other hands* file), the options the six need: a work-jacket cuff (Mateo, charcoal), a blazer cuff (Leila, cream), a short sleeve (Marcus, navy, bare forearms), a ribbed bomber cuff (Jas, olive) and a wrist hair tie (Jas); then wire the six to them through buildDriverArms options from the cast catalog (the one source of truth). Proof: seat-view frames of all six in the Rossini GT, Day, 390x844 (phone viewport copy, DPR 3) and 1280x720, and steering to full lock both ways with no clipping or sleeve popping. STEP 5, smoothness (the owner: no laggy or glitchy first person with the arms): headless SwiftShader on this loaded machine gives about 40 frames per 120 s desktop run, so one run cannot resolve 10 % at p95. Measure with tests/cast-perf.mjs as 3 ALTERNATING pairs (base, ours, base, ours, base, ours; base = a clean build of 5cf7212), 60 s each, desktop 1280x720 High and the phone profile (390x844, DPR 3, isMobile, CDP CPU throttle 4); report every run and the load average. PASS = draw calls and triangles within 2 % of base (more only if the face/hair detail needs it on HD/Ultra, never on Low; state it), the median per-run p50 within +10 %, the median per-run p95 within +10 % or inside the base's own run-to-run spread (state it), no heap growth; fix any real regression at its source. Build the base in a temporary detached worktree (git worktree add --detach /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/tmp-base/b5cf7212 5cf7212; symlink node_modules from /home/user/Claude/tsu-live/top-speed-ultra/node_modules; npm run build there) and remove it with 'git worktree remove' afterwards; never touch tsu-live or any other worktree's files. In the same base worktree run 'npm test -- --only=phone' once (not at the same time as ours) to settle whether 'sky camera: a sharp live picture inside its frame' (failed twice on cast A) also fails on the base: if yes, record it as pre-existing; if only ours, fix it. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (exactly one data-build="owner-test"); npm run store:check (no new problems vs the base); npm test -- --only=boot,phone,venues,cast,cast-seat,cast-seat-phone,cast-venues (each run under 20 minutes; split if needed); re-shoot all six beside their sheets (node tests/cast-shoot.mjs, then python3 tests/cast-sheets.py /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters) as -fx images (keep the first-pass images as BEFORE); heads at yaw 0/45/90; each venue's crowd at 1280x720 at game distance and one close third-person frame; the picker at 390x844 and 1450x767. Look at every image you cite with the Read tool and say plainly what is still short of the sheets. Honest: stylised real-time 3D on a phone, not photoreal. Log it in PROJECT_OC_PROGRESS.md (with the perf table) and PROJECT_OC_CAST.md (defect list: fixed / remaining), and in PROJECT_OC_HANDOFF.md mark the six characters' Fable prompt as taken by this pass. The rest of the cast-A brief below still stands for the parts already built (keep them working; the regression checks stay and must pass); where this pass's text is more specific, this pass wins. CAST-A BRIEF: THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~12:30 PM PT): "make there be 6 characters to choose from 3 being male and 3 female that ChatGPT can generate images for you to accurately and realistically use for this game" (later: 'realistically' means usable, not photoreal). The owner generated the reference sheets: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/ (roster.md has the names, ages, builds, outfits and notes; each 0N-name/ folder has body-sheet.webp = front/three-quarter/side/back A-pose and face-sheet.webp = front/profile/three-quarter smile). The six: 01 Mateo Reyes (27, 175 cm, stocky), 02 Danny Tran (31, 172 cm, slim, glasses), 03 Marcus Bell (38, 188 cm, muscular, shaved head, beard, scar on his RIGHT eyebrow, sunglasses on head), 04 Leila Farahani (29, 168 cm, wavy shoulder-length hair, hoops, blazer), 05 Jas Cruz (24, 160 cm, high ponytail, cropped bomber), 06 Kate Morgan (35, 175 cm, freckles, low ponytail, denim shirt, cargo pants). BUILD: (1) src/onfoot/cast.ts (new, ours): the six as presets for the existing people builder (src/onfoot/people: buildPerson, preset, PRESETS, PersonOptions, Look, Garment, Accessories), matching the sheets as closely as the stylised real-time look allows (honest: stylised 3D on a phone, not photoreal). (2) Missing builder features, ADDITIVE ONLY, in src/onfoot/people/* (agreed with the session that owns it): new hair styles (high ponytail, low ponytail, skin fade with textured top, side-part undercut, shoulder-length waves), garments (bomber, blazer, overshirt, work jacket, henley, cargo pants, chino shorts, work pants, sandals, deck shoes, low heels, chunky sneakers, boots) and accessories (glasses, sunglasses on the head, thin chain, hoop earrings, watch, hair tie) behind NEW parameter values; existing defaults, presets and the public API unchanged; avoid face.ts, masks.ts and skin.ts (another branch changes them; if a face feature truly needs them, say so instead). (3) A character picker ON THE MAIN MENU SCREEN (owner, Nov 11 ~5:35 PM PT: 'implementing into the main menu screen too'): a prominent Character entry on the main menu showing the chosen character's portrait and name, opening the picker; also reachable from the garage. The picker: six cards with each character's three-quarter smile portrait (cropped from face-sheet.webp, compressed WebP at most ~40 KB each, inlined) plus a live 3D turntable of the selected one; the choice is saved in the profile; default = keep today's player look until the player picks. (4) The chosen character is the player's avatar on foot in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time (inside the game through src/onfoot/embed.ts, and the standalone pages), and the driving hands take their skin tone through the hands' public setTone(hex) (no edits to src/preview/hands*). Phone-cheap: LOD via the builder's own budget; no per-frame allocation. Our own names; no real brands or logos on clothing. ADD a regression check: the six presets build within budget, the picker saves and restores the choice, the venue avatar matches the choice, the hands' tone follows. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (owner-test mark kept); npm test -- --only=boot,phone,venues and the new check; renders of each character front/side/back beside the same views cropped from its body sheet, and the head beside the face sheet, into tests/out/cast/; picker frames at 390x844 and 1450x767; one frame of a chosen character in each venue. THE OWNER'S MASTER BRIEF (uploaded 2026-11-11 ~1:25 PM PT; read ALL of it: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/MASTER_PROMPT.md) GOVERNS where it is more specific. Its IDs are technical labels; keep our names: M01 = Marcus Bell, M02 = Mateo Reyes, M03 = Danny Tran, F01 = Jas Cruz, F02 = Leila Farahani, F03 = Kate Morgan. Its 'nine PNGs' and character_roster.json were NOT attached (only the brief); we have MORE: a body sheet and a face sheet for all six (use them; do not claim any other file was inspected). Mismatches to record, not blend: Marcus's scar is on his RIGHT eyebrow in both images (text says left: follow the images); Mateo's jacket is drawn zip-front (text says open). THIS LANE (cast A) ADDS, per that brief: (5) ONE data-driven character catalog (cast.ts or a JSON it reads, in the project's own format): stable ID, name, portrait reference, the people-builder preset/params (our 'mesh and material references'), height and proportion data, wardrobe slots, animation config, unlock category ('base' for the six; 'pack' reserved). (6) NPC REUSE: the six are the ONLY human appearance archetypes for the current NPCs: rebuild Lot 57's and Stoppage Time's crowds and staff (src/onfoot/lot57/npcs.ts and crowd-worker.ts; src/onfoot/venues/sportsbar/crowd.ts, crew.ts, house.ts, life.ts; not people/*) from the six base looks with variety from wardrobe tints, compatible accessory choices, routes, schedules, idle and conversation timing, keeping each face, skin tone, defining hair and proportions recognisable, and avoid identical copies side by side; keep the crowd budgets, LODs and pooling. Honest labels ('Simulated crowd') stay. (7) A FUTURE TWO-CHARACTER PACK scaffold only: one catalog entry in src/store/catalog.json for a pair (one man, one woman), available: false, ONE configurable price with a caveat that the final price is undecided ($5 or $10 for the pair), a 'pack' unlock category in the cast catalog with NO identities shipped and nothing in the NPC pool; the store stays in test mode. (8) Write PROJECT_OC_CAST.md: the catalog and asset status (what exists: procedural presets, no imported meshes; missing pieces), mismatches, what this lane changed, verified results, the highest-impact remaining visual defects, and the next task (cast B: the full drive-park-exit-walk-enter-interact-leave-drive-reload loop and a graphics pass on the six). Extra proof for these: frames of each venue's crowd showing the six-look variety at 1280x720; the regression check also asserts the NPC pool only uses the six base looks and the pack is not for sale. (9) THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~1:30 PM PT): "make sure the driver matches to the player as well too". The game already has a driver choice: src/game/drivers.ts (DRIVERS archetypes, presentation m/f, SKINS, lookFor() -> DriverLook: skin tone, sleeve colour or rolled sleeves, gloves, watch, nails), which builds the cockpit's arms (src/game/vehicle/PlayerCar.ts buildDriverArms({look, presentation, nails, quality}) from src/preview/hands) and Lot 57's on-foot avatar (src/onfoot/lot57/driver.ts readDriver from tsu.settings). Make the chosen CHARACTER the driver everywhere, from ONE source of truth (the cast catalog + the saved choice): the cockpit arms and hands (skin tone, the outfit's own sleeves: Mateo's charcoal work-jacket cuffs, Danny's grey overshirt rolled to the forearm with his steel watch, Marcus's bare forearms below a navy short sleeve, Leila's cream blazer cuffs, Jas's olive bomber ribbed cuffs and her wrist hair tie, Kate's faded denim rolled to the elbow; nails per presentation), any driver figure visible from the hood or chase cameras, the on-foot avatar in BOTH venues (in-game mount and standalone pages), and the seat-view frames. The driver ARCHETYPE and its ability (Clear Path, Focus Time, Grip: DRIVERS in drivers.ts) stay a separate gameplay choice and work exactly as today: the character replaces only the APPEARANCE part (presentation, skin tone, outfit); the six are cosmetic and give no gameplay difference. Fold the old presentation/skin choice into the character picker (keep old saves working: map a saved presentation+skin to the closest character, documented). Bought driver styles (Night Shift, Golden Hour, Canyon Run) still apply on top (gloves, watch, sleeves) when equipped: document the rule. Use only the hands' public API (buildDriverArms options, setTone); if a sleeve or accessory the six need is missing in hands*, do NOT edit hands*: list it for the other session and use the closest existing option. Proof: seat-view frames (Day, 390x844 and 1280x720) of the hands for all six characters in the Rossini GT, and a regression assertion that the arms' look follows the chosen character. THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~5:45 PM PT): "make sure graphics are insane for both the steering wheel and characters and make sure it doesn't have any laggy graphics or act glitchy when 1st person POV with the arms and stuff". So: (a) TOP visual quality on HD and Ultra (physically based materials with real detail: stitching, Alcantara nap, carbon weave under clear coat, brushed and machined metal, crisp emissive lines; for people: skin shading, hair shapes, cloth folds and fabric) while Low stays cheap for phones; (b) the FIRST-PERSON views with the arms (the driving seat view, and any first-person on-foot view) must be smooth and glitch-free: no hand or arm clipping through the rim, spokes or centre while steering to full lock both ways, no sleeve or wrist popping, no z-fighting or flicker on the wheel, centre or cluster, no LOD popping in view, no texture shimmer (mipmaps, anisotropy), no per-frame allocation. MEASURE IT: a 120 s seat-view drive with steering, on the phone profile (390x844, DPR 3, isMobile, Chrome DevTools Protocol Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate 4) and on desktop 1280x720: report p50/p95/p99 frame time, long tasks over 50 ms, draw calls and triangles (window.__game stats or renderer.info) and the JS heap at start and end; the same on the base under the same conditions; the result must be no worse than +10 % p95 frame time and show no heap growth; fix any regression at its source. Put the table in the progress entry.

commit.how: HEAD has two local commits on top of 5cf7212: 224a906 (the cast-A build) and the builder's merge of origin/fable/face-r3-wip; commit the reviewed work on top of them. claude/cast has no upstream yet: push with 'git push -u origin claude/cast'. The commit message says the branch now carries cast A, the merged face rounds 1-3 (unjudged before, judged now as part of this pass) and this graphics pass.
